active_questions.text: How should the Great Library make questions visible, composable, continuously updated, and connected to evidence and approved action, without becoming the corpus warehouse or execution runtime?
Does popularity identify the software the world actually depends on, or does it systematically mismeasure it?
Which available model should own each recurring work shape after quality, reliability, tool use, latency, quota, and cost are evaluated together?
How should the information organ continuously gather, preserve, query, and push valuable evidence into authorized agent workflows and self-improvement loops?
What changes would make the complete provider-neutral SISO agent layer ten times more effective per unit of time, attention, and compute?
For a named software primitive, which implementation is best for the stated context, and is it safe and valuable to reuse, vendor, or learn from?
Which categories, techniques, and projects are gaining real momentum, what mechanisms explain the change, and what does the acceleration predict next?
How should the complete agent workspace be designed across code layout, agent architecture, memory, enforcement, and agent-generated user interfaces?

routing.note: Provider and model read from the gateway request log, not from a banner or a config label.

library_snapshot.name: Whole Library V36 — Foundry Agency OS Coverage Inventory

questions.title: The Agent Workspace
questions.decision_to_change: How to lay out a new agent workspace — what to enforce mechanically, what to leave to convention, and which patterns to refuse to repeat.
questions.answer_shape: Evidence-graded principles, reference architectures, rejected patterns, and tests that distinguish universal findings from SISO preferences.

questions.title: 10× the Agent Layer
questions.decision_to_change: Where to spend the next unit of agent-layer engineering effort: fixing an existing path's economics versus substituting a model or harness.
questions.answer_shape: A ranked leverage map whose recommendations each carry measurements, external analogues, an experiment, and a falsifiable success threshold.

questions.title: Best Software Primitive
questions.decision_to_change: Whether to build, vendor, reuse, or learn from an existing implementation of a named primitive.
questions.answer_shape: A context-specific ranked shortlist with interface fit, evidence grade, rights gate, adoption cost, and explicit reasons not to choose each candidate.

questions.title: Where the Field Is Moving
questions.decision_to_change: Where to direct research attention and which techniques to adopt early versus wait out.
questions.answer_shape: A ranked movement map with observed deltas, causal hypotheses, confidence, leading indicators, and dated predictions that can later be scored.

questions.title: The Information Organ
questions.decision_to_change: Whether to trust a published Library number without re-deriving it, and whether an evidence path is sound enough to attach to a standing question.
questions.answer_shape: A verified operating architecture with explicit ownership, freshness contracts, query primitives, feedback loops, failure modes, and observed end-to-end receipt

questions.title: Model Routing Evidence
questions.decision_to_change: Which model owns each recurring work shape, and whether an observed cost gap justifies changing the model or fixing the gateway path it was measured through.
questions.answer_shape: A versioned scenario-by-model routing matrix plus a machine-readable table, evidence grade per cell, and explicit re-evaluation triggers.

questions.title: The God Questions Observatory
questions.decision_to_change: Which registry fields, Library projections, evidence interfaces, and action-return contracts should become the standard infrastructure for every SISO God Question?
questions.answer_shape: A versioned God Questions operating architecture with a generated Observatory, machine-readable question-program contract, evidence and action-return interfaces
